body:
- Pipeline for an AI stock-picking playbook (India): Step 1 fundamental screen (latest quarter EPS & sales growth ≥ 25% YoY, 3-yr EPS CAGR ≥ 20-25%, ROE ≥ 15-17%, low pledge, adequate liquidity) → Step 2 technical gate (Trend Template pass, RS percentile ≥ 80, within 25% of 52-week high) → Step 3 market regime (Nifty 500 above rising 50/200-DMA; no distribution cluster) → Step 4 entry on base/VCP pivot with volume ≥1.5× average or on an earnings-gap EP → Step 5 risk: 0.5-1% equity risk, stop ≤ 8%, portfolio heat ≤ 6%, trail with 20/50-DMA, sell partial at 2-3R.
- Pure-momentum (Qullamaggie, Nifty200 Momentum 30) works without fundamentals but with higher turnover and crash risk; adding the fundamental filter mainly reduces "junk" momentum and pump-driven small-caps, a particular risk in Indian SME/small-cap segments.

`insight:piotroski-f-score` | 2026-11-19 | tickers: - | confidence: single-source

Piotroski (2000) 9 binary tests for cheap (high book-to-market) stocks. Profitability: ROA > 0; CFO > 0; ROA improving; CFO > net income (accrual check). Leverage/liquidity: long-term debt/assets falling; current ratio rising; no new equity issued. Efficiency: gross margin rising; asset turnover rising. Scores: 8-9 = strong, 0-2 (often <=3) = weak. Original result: within the top book-to-market quintile (1976-1996 US), buying high-F and shorting low-F earned ~23% a year; most low-F firms were the ones that later delisted or were distressed. Out-of-sample evidence is mixed: European studies find ~10%/yr high-minus-low spreads; some US post-publication and China A-share tests find little or none. Use: as a value-trap filter, not an alpha engine -- a 'cheap' stock with F <= 3, CFO < PAT and new equity issuance (Yes Bank 2019, Credit Suisse 2022, Jet 2018, Future Retail 2019) behaves like a trap. Pair with M-score (manipulation) and Z-score (distress).

**Links:** part_of -> `insight:value-trap-patterns`, similar_to -> `insight:weak-factor-folklore`
**Sources:** <https://researchworks.creighton.edu/esploro/outputs/journalArticle/Value-Stocks-and-Accounting-Screens-Has/991006117468602656> ; <https://epub.uni-regensburg.de/44019/1/Walksh%C3%A4usl2020_Article_PiotroskiSFSCOREInternationalE.pdf> ; <https://seekingalpha.com/article/4407684-why-piotroskis-f-score-no-longer-works>

`insight:group-contagion-pledge-cycles` · confidence: verified

Across the 43 group profiles reviewed (Nov-2026), the worst minority outcomes (ADAG, Essel, Future, Jaypee, Videocon, Lanco, GVK, Srei, Singh brothers) shared one structure: the promoter borrowed outside the listed company -- against its shares, or through cross-guarantees -- to fund unrelated, capital-hungry ventures (power, infra, real estate, telecom, oil). The trigger is usually an outside credit event, not the business itself: the 2008 crisis, the 2013-14 infra bust, IL&FS (Sep-2018, which froze MF/NBFC loans against shares), and COVID (2020). Pledge cycles repeat even in good groups: Emami pledged, sold ~10% in Feb-2019 to cut group debt, and a fresh ~4.95% pledge appeared in Jan-2026; Bajaj Consumer's promoters had ~70% of their stake pledged in Dec-2018 to support the sugar/power side before cutting it to zero in Oct-2019; JSW and GMR carry long-running encumbrance. Contagion is group-wide: when one company defaults, lenders cut lines to all of them, pledges get invoked, and the stocks fall together regardless of each one's fundamentals (Essel 2019: Zee, Dish, Zee Media, Siti; ADAG 2018-19). Rules: (1) count pledges across all group listed companies plus promoter holdco debt; (2) a rising pledge in a bull market is borrowing against inflated collateral; (3) a pledge cut by selling stake (Emami 2019, BAJAJCON 2019, Adani 2023) helps, but check where the money went; (4) the cycle tends to come back at the next credit tightening. Complements insight:promoter-pledge-group-contagion.

Sources: <https://business-standard.com/article/companies/emami-promoters-sell-10-stake-to-pare-group-debt-pledged-shares-119021801092_1.html> · <https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/companies/promoters-sell-22-stake-in-bajaj-consumer-care-for-rs-700-crore-119101501423_1.html> · <https://www.moneylife.in/article/sebi-bars-former-zee-executives-subhash-chandra-punit-goenka-from-securities-market-for-1-year/81233.html> · <https://filingreader.com/news-wire/mumbai/2025-11-14/gmr-enterprises-pledges-shares-in-gmr-power-and-urban-infra>

- **Base-rate reasoning:** Coin-flip for landing above a guidance midpoint absent track record (~50%).
- **Resolution rule:** YES if Five Below's reported FY2026 (year ending ~Jan-2027) comparable sales increase (Q4 FY26 earnings release) ≥ +11.0%.
